raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

On the V2 model runner, non-last PP stages snapshot outgoing intermediate tensors into one preallocated send buffer and send the snapshot instead of the live outputs, so the next forward no longer waits for the previous step's NCCL send.

- Engages only on the V2 runner, PP > 1, non-last ranks; buffer sized from the profile run's outgoing payload and charged to the KV budget.
- No new flags or env vars; the V1 runner is untouched.

## Claims

- **Stall-behind-send eliminated** on every non-last stage profiled (see table).
- **p50 TTFT −5.7% (median of 5 rounds) at 0.85× capacity** on MiniMax-M3.1-Flash PP2, prefill-heavy open loop; no consistent gain at ≤0.75×, ~+3% at ≥0.95×.
- Saturated throughput −2.7% on average, within ±5% noise.
- Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 (dummy weights): stall removed, TTFT flat — the freed time does not reach the critical path for every model/step structure.

## Validation

### Serving A/B

Same build, buffer enabled vs disabled (via an eval-only depth knob, **not** part of this PR — here the buffer is always depth 1 when it engages). MiniMax-M3.1-Flash PP2, real weights, NVFP4 KV; 100K shared prefix + 2–8K new tokens, output len 1, Poisson arrivals at fixed fractions of measured capacity; prefix cache reset + primed per pass, second pass kept; interleaved rounds with rotated order.

p50 TTFT, PR vs upstream within the same round; last column is the median:

| load | R1 | R2 | R3 | R4 | R5 | median |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0.6 × C | −0.8% | +12.2% | −0.3% | — | — | −0.3% |
| 0.75 × C | −9.6% | −5.5% | +0.0% | +1.9% | +3.4% | +0.0% |
| 0.85 × C | −5.7% | +1.0% | −6.3% | −1.3% | −9.6% | **−5.7%** |
| 0.95 × C | +2.7% | +3.8% | +3.1% | +0.0% | −1.0% | +2.7% |

nsys stall analysis (window at 0.85 × capacity; "stall" = compute-idle time ended by a send completing):

| model / config | stage | stalled behind send: upstream → PR |
|---|---|---:|
| MiniMax-M3.1-Flash PP2 | 0 | 5.9–9.7% → 0.0% (6 buffered arms) |
| Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 PP2 | 0 | 7.0% → 0.0% |
| Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 PP4 | 0 / 1 / 2 | 10.4 / 7.2 / 5.8% → 0 / 0 / 0.3% |

### Correctness

- New distributed chain tests (`tests/distributed/test_pp_send_buffer.py`): PP2 and PP4 chains, varying per-step payload sizes, stages taking turns lagging; asserts payloads arrive intact while senders overwrite their outputs every step.
  `python -m pytest tests/distributed/test_pp_send_buffer.py -v` → 2 passed in 55.90s (PP2 and PP4 chains, 4× B300)
- GSM8K with real weights: pending; required before leaving draft.

## Details

- Root cause: an NCCL send completes only when the peer posts its receive, which the next stage does after its own previous forward. Sending live outputs makes the next forward wait, since it would overwrite the send's source (CUDA-graph outputs are static; relayed aux hidden states alias the persistent receive buffer). The snapshot moves that wait to the next buffer copy. This pays only when the slower stage alternates step to step; uniform full batches see no change.
- One buffer per sending rank, sized from the profile run and charged to the memory profile, so KV-cache sizing accounts for it. Cost: one payload-sized device copy per step on non-last stages. Depth 2 was evaluated and adds nothing.
- Not a duplicate: #53948 defers sampled-result receives; #64385/#64350 add stage-local DBO graphs; #63745 changes PP boundaries; #41501 shrinks residual payloads; #53102 types PP transport. None isolates outgoing-send storage.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""PP send buffers carry every step's tensors intact through a PP chain while
+senders overwrite their outputs every step (as CUDA graph outputs are reused),
+middle stages relay views of their receive buffer (as MRV2 relays aux hidden
+states), sizes vary, and stages take turns lagging behind."""
+
+import pytest
+import ray
+import torch
+
+from vllm.distributed.parallel_state import get_pp_group, get_tp_group
+from vllm.v1.worker.pp_send_buffer import PPSendBuffer, packed_nbytes
+
+from ..utils import (
+    init_test_distributed_environment,
+    multi_gpu_test,
+    multi_process_parallel,
+)
+
+MAX_ROWS, WIDTH, STEPS = 4096, 1024, 40
+
+
+def _fill(step: int, rank: int, key: int) -> int:
+    return (step * 7 + rank * 3 + key) % 120
+
+
+@ray.remote(num_gpus=1, max_calls=1)
+def send_buffer_chain_worker(
+    monkeypatch, tp_size, pp_size, rank, distributed_init_port
+):
+    torch.accelerator.set_device_index(rank)
+    init_test_distributed_environment(1, pp_size, rank, distributed_init_port)
+    pp_group = get_pp_group()
+    first, last = pp_group.is_first_rank, pp_group.is_last_rank
+
+    def zeros() -> torch.Tensor:
+        return torch.zeros(MAX_ROWS, WIDTH, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+
+    # Every step's outputs land in the same storage.
+    outputs = {"hidden_states": zeros(), "residual": zeros()}
+    # Persistent receive buffer, relayed onward as views.
+    relayed = zeros()
+    payload = dict(outputs) if first else dict(outputs, relay=relayed)
+    send_buffer = None if last else PPSendBuffer(packed_nbytes(payload), "cuda")
+
+    lag = torch.randn(4096, 4096, device="cuda")
+    for step in range(STEPS):
+        n = (MAX_ROWS, 1, 1337, 512)[step % 4]
+        if not first:
+            received = pp_group.recv_tensor_dict(all_gather_group=get_tp_group())
+            expected = {"hidden_states": 0, "residual": 1}
+            for key, offset in expected.items():
+                want = _fill(step, rank - 1, offset)
+                assert torch.equal(
+                    received[key], torch.full_like(received[key], want)
+                ), (step, key)
+            if rank > 1:
+                want = _fill(step, rank - 2, 0)
+                assert torch.equal(
+                    received["relay"], torch.full_like(received["relay"], want)
+                ), (step, "relay")
+            relayed[:n].copy_(received["hidden_states"])
+        if last:
+            continue
+        # Stages lag in turns: a slow sender lets receivers run ahead, a slow
+        # receiver makes the next snapshot wait for its send.
+        if (step + rank) % 3 == 0:
+            for _ in range(20):
+                lag @ lag
+        for offset, key in enumerate(outputs):
+            outputs[key][:n].fill_(_fill(step, rank, offset))
+        tensors = {key: value[:n] for key, value in outputs.items()}
+        if not first:
+            tensors["relay"] = relayed[:n]
+        assert send_buffer is not None
+        send_buffer.send(tensors, pp_group, get_tp_group())
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    # A stage's last metadata send completes only once the next stage
+    # receives it, so no stage may exit before the chain is done.
+    torch.distributed.barrier(group=pp_group.cpu_group)
+
+
+@multi_gpu_test(num_gpus=2)
+def test_pp_send_buffer_pp2(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch):
+    multi_process_parallel(monkeypatch, 1, 2, send_buffer_chain_worker)
+
+
+@multi_gpu_test(num_gpus=4)
+def test_pp_send_buffer_pp4(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch):
+    multi_process_parallel(monkeypatch, 1, 4, send_buffer_chain_worker)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Dedicated storage for a PP stage's outgoing intermediate tensors.
+
+An NCCL send completes only when the next stage posts its receive, and the
+sender's next forward would overwrite the outputs being sent (CUDA graph
+outputs are static; relayed aux states alias the receive buffer). Sending this
+snapshot moves the wait to the next copy into the buffer.
+"""
+
+from typing import Any
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.distributed.parallel_state import GroupCoordinator, Handle
+from vllm.utils.math_utils import round_up
+
+
+def _layout(tensors: dict[str, Any]) -> tuple[dict[str, int], int]:
+    """Aligned byte offset of each tensor in the buffer, and the bytes used."""
+    offsets: dict[str, int] = {}
+    end = 0
+    for key, value in tensors.items():
+        if isinstance(value, torch.Tensor):
+            offsets[key] = round_up(end, 256)
+            end = offsets[key] + value.nbytes
+    return offsets, end
+
+
+def packed_nbytes(tensors: dict[str, Any]) -> int:
+    """Buffer bytes needed to send `tensors`."""
+    return _layout(tensors)[1]
+
+
+class PPSendBuffer:
+    def __init__(self, nbytes: int, device: torch.device) -> None:
+        self.buffer = torch.empty(nbytes, dtype=torch.uint8, device=device)
+        self._send_work: list[Handle] = []
+
+    def send(
+        self,
+        tensors: dict[str, Any],
+        pp_group: GroupCoordinator,
+        all_gather_group: GroupCoordinator | None,
+    ) -> None:
+        offsets, nbytes = _layout(tensors)
+        devices = {tensors[k].device for k in offsets}
+        if devices - {self.buffer.device}:
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                f"PP send tensors on {devices}, send buffer on {self.buffer.device}"
+            )
+        if nbytes > self.buffer.numel():
+            shapes = {k: tuple(v.shape) for k, v in tensors.items() if k in offsets}
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                f"PP send of {nbytes} bytes {shapes} exceeds the "
+                f"{self.buffer.numel()}-byte send buffer sized from the profile run"
+            )
+        # The previous snapshot's sends must have read the buffer. This is a
+        # stream wait, so the CPU keeps going.
+        for handle in self._send_work:
+            handle.wait()
+        staged: dict[str, Any] = {}
+        for key, value in tensors.items():
+            if key not in offsets:
+                staged[key] = value
+                continue
+            start = offsets[key]
+            view = self.buffer[start : start + value.nbytes]
+            staged[key] = view.view(value.dtype).view(value.shape)
+            staged[key].copy_(value)
+        handles = pp_group.isend_tensor_dict(staged, all_gather_group=all_gather_group)
+        # The metadata handle is reaped by the group coordinator.
+        self._send_work = handles[1:]
